findings: The source mentions a matrix minimum path and DP/Dijkstra but does not preserve movement or weight constraints, so the candidate makes those contracts explicit before choosing an algorithm.
For right/down movement, the candidate implements the DAG dynamic-programming recurrence and explains one-dimensional state compression.
For four-direction movement with non-negative cell costs, the candidate models the grid as a weighted graph and uses Dijkstra with a stale-entry guard and explicit rejection of negative costs.

Independent review matched the DP method against a separate two-dimensional oracle on 12000 random signed grids and Dijkstra against Floyd-Warshall on 2500 random non-negative grids, plus singleton/start-cost and negative-weight boundary checks.

The prior review attempt failed only because the evidence object exposed two boundary-test records while the audit contract requires at least three; this remediation records the already-tested negative-weight boundary explicitly and re-runs it independently.
